      <title>Linux Foundation Newsletter: November 2026</title>
      <link>https://www.linuxfoundation.org/blog/linux-foundation-newsletter-november-2026</link>
      <description><div class="hs-featured-image-wrapper"> 
 <a href="https://www.linuxfoundation.org/blog/linux-foundation-newsletter-november-2026?hsLang=en" title="" class="hs-featured-image-link"> <img src="https://www.linuxfoundation.org/hubfs/Blog%20%2824%29-2.png" alt="Linux Foundation Newsletter: November 2026" class="hs-featured-image" style="width:auto !important; max-width:50%; float:left; margin:0 15px 15px 0;"> </a> 
</div> 
<p style="font-weight: bold;">Welcome to the November 2026 edition of the Linux Foundation Newsletter!</p> 
<p>LF Education’s <a href="https://training.linuxfoundation.org" class="sa-set-id">Black Friday sale</a> runs November 27 through December 4, with savings of up to 65% on training and certifications. Also new is the <a href="https://training.linuxfoundation.org/certification/certified-kubernetes-network-engineer-ckne">Certified Kubernetes Network Engineer (CKNE)</a> certification and its <a href="https://training.linuxfoundation.org/certification/ckne-certification-pathway">Certification Pathway</a>, and you can sign up to be notified when registration opens for the <a href="https://training.linuxfoundation.org/certification/secure-ai-associate-saia/">Secure AI Associate (SAIA)</a> exam.</p> 
<p>This month’s biggest announcements include a new open source project for AI agent identity and a milestone for the Agentic AI Foundation. The Linux Foundation welcomed <a href="https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/linux-foundation-welcomes-agent-name-service-to-bring-verifiable-identity-and-discovery-to-ai-agents?hsLang=en">Agent Name Service (ANS)</a>, which builds on DNS to verify and discover AI agents. <span><a href="https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/agentic-ai-foundation-announces-four-new-projects-agent-skills-open-responses-openenv-and-opensandbox?hsLang=en">AAIF added four projects</a></span> (Agent Skills, Open Responses, OpenEnv, and OpenSandbox), bringing it to 10 hosted projects, and passed 300 members in its first year. The <span><a href="https://www.cncf.io/announcements/2026/11/10/cncf-hits-major-milestones-with-global-community-growth-record-industry-investment-and-a-new-generation-of-projects-to-build-ai-systems-in-production/">CNCF now hosts 231 projects</a></span>, with <span><a href="https://www.cncf.io/announcements/2026/11/10/cloud-native-computing-foundation-announces-kubevirt-graduation/">KubeVirt</a></span> and <span><a href="https://cloudnativenow.com/uncategorized/cncf-graduates-nats-messaging-and-streaming-project/">NATS</a></span> graduating this month.</p> 
<p>LF Research published four reports. <span><a href="https://www.linuxfoundation.org/research/the-2026-state-of-open-source-in-financial-services?hsLang=en">The 2026 State of Open Source in Financial Services</a></span> found a 63% year-over-year increase in GitHub commits from financial institutions. <a href="https://www.linuxfoundation.org/hubfs/Research%20Reports/State%20of%20AI%20Impact%20on%20Software%20Security%20and%20Cybersecurity%202026.pdf?hsLang=en">The AI impact on cybersecurity report</a> found that 3 in 5 teams ship code faster than security reviews can keep up. A third finds that the future depends on VMs and containers running together, and the fourth, <span><a href="https://www.linuxfoundation.org/research/2026-state-of-commercial-open-source?hsLang=en">State of Commercial Open Source 2026</a></span>, draws on 225 founders and leaders. LF Research and CNCF are also fielding a <span><a href="https://www.linuxfoundation.org/research/surveys/2026-state-of-the-neocloud-survey?hsLang=en">3-minute survey on neocloud adoption</a></span>.</p> 
<p>You’ll also find a recap of the industry challenge LF Europe co-led at the World Open Innovation Conference in Kaunas, Lithuania, plus project news that ranges from agentic AI to telecom and embedded systems.</p> 
<p style="color: #434343;"><span style="color: #000000;"><span style="font-weight: bold;">&gt;&gt; &nbsp;</span><span style="font-weight: normal;"><span style="font-weight: bold;">Read on</span> for even more news, research, and opportunities from across the Linux Foundation.</span></span></p></description>

      <title>Navigating Open Source Software Development in the Generative AI Era: Balancing Velocity and Community Health</title>
      <link>https://www.linuxfoundation.org/blog/navigating-open-source-software-development-in-the-generative-ai-era-balancing-velocity-and-community-health</link>
      <description><div class="hs-featured-image-wrapper"> 
 <a href="https://www.linuxfoundation.org/blog/navigating-open-source-software-development-in-the-generative-ai-era-balancing-velocity-and-community-health?hsLang=en" title="" class="hs-featured-image-link"> <img src="https://www.linuxfoundation.org/hubfs/Research%20Reports/Navigating-Open-Source-Software-Development-in-the-Generative-AI-Era-Featured-Image.png" alt="Navigating Open Source Software Development in the Generative AI Era: Balancing Velocity and Community Health" class="hs-featured-image" style="width:auto !important; max-width:50%; float:left; margin:0 15px 15px 0;"> </a> 
</div> 
<p>Over the past three decades, open source communities have absorbed one massive technological shift after another: the emergence of the web, the mobile revolution, and the rise of cloud native infrastructure. Through each transition, our ecosystem adapted, strengthened its collaborative norms, and grew more resilient. Yet generative AI introduces a fundamentally distinct dynamic, directly affecting the heart of how project communities function.</p></description>

</div> 
<p style="color: #434343; font-weight: bold;">Welcome to the October 2026 edition of the Linux Foundation Newsletter</p> 
<p><span style="color: #000000;">Cybersecurity Awareness Month is ending, and LF Education is discounting training for a limited time. You can<a href="https://hubs.la/Q04B3NYW0" style="color: #000000;"><u>save 40%</u></a> on eligible cybersecurity training and certifications, and you can save 35% on other training and certifications. A THRIVE-ONE Annual subscription is 30% off.</span></p> 
<p><span style="color: #000000;">This month's biggest announcements include a new Platinum Member and two new foundations. AWS<a href="https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/aws-becomes-a-platinum-member-of-the-linux-foundation-deepening-commitment-to-open-source?hsLang=en" style="color: #000000;"><u>became a Platinum Member</u></a> of the Linux Foundation, after more than a decade of taking part in LF projects. The Linux Foundation launched the<a href="https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/linux-foundation-launches-build-foundation-to-sustain-large-scale-multi-language-build-and-test-systems?hsLang=en" style="color: #000000;"><u>BUILD Foundation</u></a>, which gives organizations that depend on Bazel a formal way to fund the project and help set its direction. The Linux Foundation also launched<a href="https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/linux-foundation-launches-opengrid-to-build-open-shared-infrastructure-for-the-worlds-electric-grid?hsLang=en" style="color: #000000;"><u>OpenGrid</u></a>, which sets shared software architecture and interoperability standards so that power grid planning tools can work together. In addition, FINOS announced that<a href="https://www.finos.org/press/major-banks-back-osera-open-source-security-standards-and-fixes" style="color: #000000;"><u>OSERA</u></a> is now operating, with support from Deutsche Bank, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, NatWest, and RBC. The first OSERA release includes secure updates for more than 50 widely used Spring and Java libraries.</span></p> 
<p><span style="color: #000000;">LF Research published nine reports this month.<a href="https://www.linuxfoundation.org/research/35-years-of-linux?hsLang=en" style="color: #000000;"><u>35 Years of Linux</u></a> follows the kernel from a hobby project to the software that now runs on 4 billion Android devices, more than 200 million servers, and all 500 of the world's top supercomputers. The 9th annual<a href="https://www.linuxfoundation.org/research/ospo-2026?hsLang=en" style="color: #000000;"><u>State of OSPOs</u></a> study looks at how open source program offices are handling AI governance. The<a href="https://www.linuxfoundation.org/research/opensearch-data-infrastructure-2026?hsLang=en" style="color: #000000;"><u>2026 Open Data Infrastructure Report</u></a> finds that openly governed data platforms are gaining ground as more organizations run AI workloads.</span></p> 
<p><span style="color: #000000;">You'll also find a recap of the Linux Foundation Member European Forum in Prague and details on the LF Education Learning Lounge at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America. The project news covers agentic AI, finance, energy, networking, security, and embedded systems.</span></p>

<p><span>Two LF Decentralized Trust (LFDT) communities—the </span><a href="https://lf-toip.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/HOME/pages/257785857/Decentralized+Trust+Graph+Working+Group"><u><span>ToIP / DIF Decentralized Trust Graph Working Group</span></u></a><span> (DTGWG) and </span><a href="https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/openvtc"><u><span>OpenVTC</span></u></a><span>, an LFDT lab—reached a major milestone at the </span><a href="https://lpc.events/event/20/contributions/2350/"><u><span>Linux Plumbers Conference</span></u></a><span> and LF Open Source Summit EU in Prague last week: demonstrating the first verifiable trust community (VTC) for open source projects.</span></p></description>
